jobs.title: Ehrenamt · remote · 4–6 Std./Woche: Finanzbuchhalter:in für den Aufbau unserer B
jobs.excerpt: Du hast jahrelang Bücher geführt und möchtest dein Wissen jetzt für das Gemeinwohl einsetzen?
jobs.description:
Du hast jahrelang Bücher geführt und möchtest dein Wissen jetzt für das Gemeinwohl einsetzen? Vielleicht bist du im (Vor-)Ruhestand, in Elternzeit oder arbeitest Teilzeit und willst fachlich am Ball bleiben. Bei uns fängst du nicht mit Altlasten an, sondern auf einem leeren Blatt: Unsere Buchhaltung gibt es noch nicht. Du baust sie mit uns auf.

Gleich vorweg: Das ist ein Ehrenamt

Die Aufgabe ist unbezahlt und begründet kein Arbeitsverhältnis. Wir suchen Menschen, die ihre Erfahrung einbringen möchten, weil ihnen die Sache wichtig ist.

Wer wir sind

Der Deutsche Hilfsbund e.V. (DEHIB) bündelt Hilfsorganisationen und bringt sie mit Menschen aus Wirtschaft, Politik und Wissenschaft zusammen, damit soziales Engagement mehr bewirkt. Wir verbinden Verbände, schaffen professionelle Strukturen und bauen bundesweit eine Plattform für gesellschaftliche Wirkung auf. Dafür brauchen wir ein solides Finanzwesen – und dich.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Buchhaltung von Grund auf mit aufbauen: Kontenrahmen, Belegwege und Abläufe gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung festlegen
  • Laufende Finanzbuchhaltung: Belege prüfen, kontieren und buchen (Debitoren, Kreditoren, Sachkonten)

· Zahlungsverkehr abwickeln

  • Konten abstimmen und bei Abschlüssen mitwirken
  • Auswertungen für Vorstand und Geschäftsführung erstellen
  • Ansprechperson für unsere operativen Bereiche und die Vereine im DEHIB sein

Zu viel für eine Person? Dann teilen wir die Aufgaben gern auf, zum Beispiel im Tandem.

Was du mitbringst

  • Mehrjährige Praxis in der Finanzbuchhaltung – ob aktuell oder aus deinem bisherigen Berufsleben
  • Idealerweise hast du schon einmal eine Buchhaltung eingerichtet oder umgestellt
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Buchhaltungssoftware und Excel
  • Sorgfalt im Umgang mit digitalen Belegen und Daten

· Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse

  • Verlässlichkeit: Du bist bereit uns regelmäßig 4–6 Stunden pro Woche zu unterstützen

Was wir dir bieten

Sinn & Gemeinnutz

  • Deine Arbeit kommt direkt dem Gemeinwohl zugute: Ein solides Finanzwesen ist die Grundlage dafür, dass Hilfe dort ankommt, wo sie gebraucht wird.
  • Du arbeitest mit Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen und gesellschaftlich etwas bewegen wollen.

Exklusives Netzwerk

  • Zugang zu einem wachsenden Netzwerk aus Wirtschaft, Politik, Wissenschaft und Non-Profit-Organisationen
  • Austausch mit Unternehmer:innen, Führungskräften und Expert:innen ganz unterschiedlicher Fachrichtungen
  • Zugriff auf das Know-how unserer angeschlossenen Organisationen und Kooperationspartner

Gestaltung & Verantwortung

  • Du baust etwas Eigenes auf, statt nur abzuarbeiten – mit viel Eigenverantwortung
  • Direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung
  • Perspektivisch die Leitung eines Teams im Finanz- und Rechnungswesen

Entwicklung & Referenz

  • Du verbindest Buchhaltung mit Organisationsentwicklung und sammelst Erfahrung im Non-Profit-Bereich
  • Eine starke Referenz: der Aufbau des Finanzwesens einer bundesweit tätigen Organisation
  • Qualifiziertes Ehrenamtszeugnis und Tätigkeitsnachweis

So arbeiten wir zusammen

  • Komplett remote mit Microsoft 365, deine Zeit teilst du dir flexibel ein
  • Klare Absprachen: Aufgaben, Zeitumfang und feste Termine im Monat halten wir in einer kurzen Ehrenamtsvereinbarung fest
  • Gute Einarbeitung, eine feste Ansprechperson und eine Kennenlernphase von zwei bis drei Monaten

So meldest du dich – ganz unkompliziert

Kein Anschreiben, kein Bewerbungsmarathon: Schreib uns in drei, vier Sätzen, was du in der Buchhaltung gemacht hast und warum dich dieses Ehrenamt reizt. Danach lernen wir uns virtuell für 30 Minuten kennen und schauen gemeinsam, ob es passt.

Case IQ is a leading B2B SaaS company in the governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) space, helping organizations build safer, more accountable workplaces. We offer a comprehensive suite of solutions that enable organizations to move from reactive approaches to proactive risk management. Our software helps teams across compliance, HR, legal, and investigations report, manage, investigate, and prevent workplace risk - including ethics violations, fraud, harassment, discrimination, security incidents, and third-party issues - so they can better protect their people, culture, and business.

Backed by over 25 years of domain expertise and trusted by Fortune 500 companies, Case IQ has supported the management of millions of cases and helped mitigate billions in financial and reputational risk.

Role Summary

We are looking for a Security Assurance Specialist to support Case IQ’s customer-facing security assurance process under the direction of the Director of Information Security. This remote-first role is a strong fit for an early-career professional who is interested in information security, customer assurance, documentation, and supporting enterprise sales within a growing security program.

In this role, you will help complete customer security questionnaires and due diligence requests, maintain an approved response and evidence library, keep the Trust Center current, and coordinate with Information Security, Compliance, Legal, Product, Engineering, IT, and Sales. While the role is remote, we are seeking candidates based in the Ottawa area.

AI-Forward Ways of Working

At Case IQ, AI is part of how we build. We look for engineers who can use AI-assisted development and agentic workflows with strong technical judgment: defining clear intent and constraints, validating outputs, protecting customer data, and keeping humans accountable for production decisions. You will help establish practical patterns for responsible AI use across discovery, design, implementation, testing, observability, and operations.

What You'll Do

  • Track customer security requests, deadlines, owners, and outstanding items so requests move forward predictably
  • Help maintain the Case IQ Trust Center by keeping published security and compliance information current and flagging gaps for review

  • Learn Case IQ’s products, security practices, and compliance commitments well enough to recognize when a request needs specialist review
  • Help document repeatable Customer Assurance workflows, response standards, and lessons learned

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 Days: Complete onboarding and build familiarity with Case IQ’s products, security documentation, compliance commitments, customer assurance process, key stakeholders, and response standards. Shadow questionnaire and customer-request work, review the response library and Trust Center, and begin drafting straightforward responses for review.
  • 60 Days: Support smaller and standard questionnaires and customer requests under close review, using approved responses and evidence. Keep request tracking current, help organize the response library, and contribute proposed Trust Center or documentation updates.
  • 90 Days: Handle routine requests with regular manager review and confidently route complex or non-standard questions to the appropriate subject-matter expert. Maintain accurate status reporting and identify recurring customer questions, content gaps, or process improvements.
  • 6 Months: Manage well-defined recurring Customer Assurance tasks with guidance, maintain accurate and current customer-facing security information, and contribute to smoother coordination between Sales and internal subject-matter experts.
  • 1 Year: Operate as a reliable Customer Assurance partner for standard requests, keep the response library and Trust Center well organized, and support continuous improvement of the customer security review process while escalating complex matters appropriately.

Who You Are

  • Early-career experience in a customer-facing, SaaS operations, security, privacy, compliance, sales operations, or related role; internships, co-op terms, or equivalent experience are welcome
  • Strong written communication skills and care with detail, including the ability to turn technical input into clear, accurate customer-facing responses
  • Good organizational and project-tracking habits, with the ability to manage several requests and deadlines with guidance
  • Interest in information security, privacy, compliance, or enterprise software, and a willingness to learn Case IQ’s products and security program
  • Comfort working with documents, spreadsheets, knowledge bases, and shared collaboration tools
  • Ability to ask thoughtful questions, identify missing information, and escalate requests that need expert review
  • Collaborative working style and the ability to build constructive relationships with Sales, Legal, Compliance, Security, Product, Engineering, and IT teams
  • Basic understanding of common security and privacy concepts, such as access control, encryption, incident response, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or data protection
  • Exercise the highest level of discretion in the handling and protection of all data and sensitive information

Assets (Nice to Have)

  • Experience assisting with security questionnaires, RFPs, customer due diligence, or Trust Center content
  • Familiarity with security and privacy frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, GDPR, or PIPEDA
  • Exposure to SaaS sales, customer success, procurement, legal operations, or compliance work

Perks and Benefits

About the Role

Entrada AI, Inc. is seeking an experienced AI Architect (Generative AI & Databricks) to join our growing team of consultants to lead the design and implementation of an enterprise GenAI platform for a marquee client.

In this role, you will architect an intelligent ingestion pipeline and an Anti-Hallucination & Zero-Inference Architecture designed to automate the triage, parameter extraction, and staging of incoming customer commercial pricing requests. You will bridge advanced LLM orchestration with production Lakehouse patterns, replacing manual data re-keying with high-throughput unstructured parsing, automated guardrail verification, an interactive Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) review cockpit built on Databricks Apps.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and oversee the end-to-end GenAI Lakehouse architecture on Databricks, transforming unstructured email threads and complex attachments into fully verified, ERP-ready tabular data.

  • Lead the development of deterministic extraction workflows on Databricks Model Serving (Claude/GPT), enforcing strict Pydantic schemas to accurately extract commercial attributes without arbitrary prose.

  • Implement a 3-layer anti-hallucination verification engine combining strict schema constraints, mandatory source citations, and PySpark string-assertion to ensure zero hallucinated data reaches production.

  • Architect and deploy an interactive Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) review application natively on Databricks Apps (Streamlit/Dash) featuring side-by-side reconciliation, manual override capabilities, and secure SSO/OBO authentication.

  • Model Gold-layer pricing staging tables and design automated batch feeds for downstream ERP consumption via Databricks SQL Warehouses and REST APIs.

  • Establish best practices for Unity Catalog governance, data lineage, error-quarantine routing, and system security across client engineering teams.

  • Create and maintain comprehensive architectural documentation, data models, and interface specifications while mentoring client teams.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Engineering, or a related field.

  • 7+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture, or applied machine learning systems.

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience designing and deploying solutions on the Databricks Lakehouse Platform (Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, Databricks Model Serving, and Databricks SQL).

  • Demonstrated experience as an Applied GenAI / LLMOps Engineer/Architect, specifically building structured extraction pipelines using function calling, Pydantic validation, and custom guardrail/citation-verification systems.

  • Proven track record parsing dirty, semi-structured, and unstructured business documents using Python and PySpark libraries (PyMuPDF, pdfplumber, OpenPyXL, BeautifulSoup4).

  • Hands-on experience developing and deploying interactive data applications using Streamlit or Dash, with specific experience deploying containerized apps natively inside Databricks Apps.

  • Strong understanding of enterprise identity and API integrations, including Microsoft Graph API, OAuth 2.0 client credential flows, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and Databricks Secret Scopes.

  • Solid background in data modeling, governance, and auditability inside Unity Catalog (handling Volumes, Delta Tables, ACLs, and row/column-level security).

  • Experience or working familiarity with downstream enterprise ERP integration patterns.

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to design resilient, production-ready systems that prevent hallucinated data from touching financial systems of record.

  • Excellent communication, consulting, and client-facing skills, with the ability to articulate complex GenAI concepts clearly to both technical teams and executive business stakeholders.

About VictoriaMetrics

We are the company behind the popular open-source, high-performance time-series database and monitoring solution: VictoriaMetrics. Fortune 500 companies rely on our products as their core monitoring infrastructure. Our technology is trusted by Adidas, Wix, Grammarly, CERN, and thousands of engineering teams worldwide.
We are self-funded, profitable, and growing — which means every enterprise deal matters, and every salesperson has genuine leverage. There is no bureaucracy between you and the market.

About the Opportunity

After six years of strong growth in Europe and North America — driven primarily by inbound and community-led demand — we are now building the enterprise sales function that will take VictoriaMetrics to the next level. This is not a role for someone looking to work an existing playbook. We are looking for a Senior Enterprise AE who can navigate complex, technical sales cycles, build executive relationships, and close deals that matter.
You will work closely with Sales leadership, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success to move enterprise accounts from first conversation to signed contract — and then expand them. The role spans new logo acquisition and expansion within existing accounts, with a strong emphasis on the US market and growing coverage across Europe and APAC.
Our buyers are engineers, SREs, DevOps leads, and infrastructure architects. They are sophisticated, skeptical of vendor hype, and deeply value technical credibility. If you enjoy selling to people who can tell when you don't know what you're talking about — and can hold your own in those conversations — this role is for you.

Our Values

We hire for a specific combination of traits. Our formula:

Impact = Ownership × Quality × Creativity × Speed × Integrity

Ownership -You act like a founder of the revenue engine — not a passenger. You own your pipeline, your accounts, and your results.

Quality -You build durable customer relationships, not fragile wins. High standards in every proposal, conversation, and follow-up.

Creativity -You find non-obvious paths to revenue. You adapt the playbook, or invent a new one, when the situation demands it.

Speed -You test, learn, and iterate quickly. You move with urgency but not at the cost of accuracy or trust.

Integrity -You do the right thing even when it costs you. You build trust with customers and colleagues — and you keep it.

We are looking for someone who embodies these values — not as a performance in interviews, but as a genuine way of working. You will be evaluated on them throughout the hiring process and in performance reviews.

What You Will Do
Own the Enterprise Sales Cycle

  • Run end-to-end sales cycles for new enterprise accounts — from outbound prospecting and inbound qualification through to commercial negotiation and close.

  • Manage complex, multi-stakeholder deals across technical champions (SREs, DevOps engineers), economic buyers, and procurement — applying MEDDIC to drive rigorous qualification throughout.

  • Develop and execute account plans for strategic targets, including stakeholder mapping, value proposition alignment, and competitive positioning.

  • Accurately forecast your pipeline and maintain a healthy, documented book of business in HubSpot.

Drive Expansion Within Existing Accounts

  • Identify and execute upsell and cross-sell opportunities within the existing customer base — from open-source adoption to VictoriaMetrics Enterprise and VictoriaLogs.

  • Partner with Customer Success to monitor account health, identify expansion signals, and ensure renewals are protected and grown.

  • Build multi-threaded relationships within strategic accounts so that no deal is dependent on a single contact.

Engage Technical Buyers with Credibility

  • Understand VictoriaMetrics products deeply enough to hold substantive conversations with engineers about architecture, performance, and TCO.

  • Articulate the value of the enterprise offering over the open-source product — not just through feature comparison, but through total cost of ownership, support, compliance, and scale arguments.

  • Work with Solutions Engineering on technical evaluations, proof-of-concepts, and competitive bakeoffs.

  • Stay current on the observability and monitoring landscape — Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Elastic, and adjacent technologies — to position VictoriaMetrics with confidence.

Contribute to the Go-To-Market System

  • Feed structured deal intelligence — objections, competitive dynamics, persona insights, pricing friction — back into Marketing, Product, and Sales leadership.

  • Collaborate with the BDR team on targeted account strategies and ensure smooth handoffs in both directions.

  • Contribute to playbook development, competitive battlecards, and sales enablement materials as the function matures.

  • Represent VictoriaMetrics at industry events, conferences, and customer meetings.

About You
Experience & Qualifications

  • 5+ years of B2B enterprise software sales, with a consistent track record of meeting or exceeding quota.

  • 3+ years selling open-source, open-core, or developer-first software — you understand how community adoption translates into commercial pipeline.

  • Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles with deal sizes of $100K+ ACV.

  • Proven ability to sell into DevOps, infrastructure, observability, or adjacent technical domains.

  • Proficiency with MEDDIC or a comparable enterprise qualification framework.

  • Hands-on with HubSpot or a comparable CRM; comfortable maintaining rigorous pipeline hygiene.

  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a meaningful advantage.

What Sets You Apart

  • Technically fluent: you can hold a substantive conversation with an SRE or infrastructure engineer without relying on a solutions engineer to translate.

  • Commercially sharp: you understand contract structure, pricing models (on-prem, SaaS, consumption), and how to navigate procurement without losing margin.

  • Strategically patient: you know when to push and when to wait. You build relationships that outlast individual deals.

  • Genuinely curious about the product: you have explored VictoriaMetrics, understand why engineers choose it, and can speak credibly about what it does and does not do.

  • Builder mindset: you are comfortable in an environment where not everything is defined. You contribute to the system, not just work within it.

Together We Will

  • Build an enterprise sales motion that scales beyond inbound — and becomes a competitive advantage for VictoriaMetrics.

  • Close deals with engineering-led organisations that are building the infrastructure of tomorrow.

  • Develop a commercial approach to the open-source-to-enterprise journey that others in the industry will study.

  • Give you the autonomy, support, and tooling to do your best work — with competitive compensation, performance bonuses, flexible hours, and a remote-first culture built on trust.

Job Title

Senior Policy Researcher

Job Category

M&P - AAPS

Job Profile

Staff - Non Union

Department

Research | Sonia Li Trottier | Peter A. Allard School of Law

The Compensation Range is the span between the minimum and maximum base salary for a position. The midpoint of the range is approximately halfway between the minimum and the maximum and represents an employee that possesses full job knowledge, qualifications and experience for the position. In the normal course, employees will be hired, transferred or promoted between the minimum and midpoint of the salary range for a job.

Job End Date

October 31, 2027

Posting End Date

October 28, 2026

Note:Applications will be accepted until 11:59 PM on the Posting End Date.

This position is expected to be filled by promotion/reassignment and is included here to inform you of its vacancy at the University.

Job Summary
The Senior Policy Researcher, under the supervision of the Director of the Canada Climate Law Initiative, will play a crucial role in leading the policy research, writing in-depth analysis, and meeting with key policymakers, regulators, and partners. The Senior Policy Researcher will be responsible for performing research and analysis, engaging with the policy and partners’ ecosystem, and providing thought leadership.

The Senior Policy Researcher identifies research opportunities, leads approved research projects, and provides high-quality research and analysis to advance CCLI's policy objectives. The position also supervises research assistants and represents CCLI in external research and policy engagement activities.

The Senior Policy Researcher will benefit from opportunities to expand their professional network, engage in cutting-edge research collaboration, and receive support from leading Canadian scholars.

The Director retains authority for approval of research projects, final research scopes, final publications and policy submissions, and commitments that would create financial, legal, contractual, or other material obligations on behalf of CCLI.

Organizational Status
The Senior Policy Researcher reports to the Director, Canada Climate Law Initiative. Works with considerable latitude under general supervision, while collaborating closely with the CCLI team. Maintains strong working relationships with Allard staff, as well as external partners. This role is visible to the external community, working with government and regulatory agencies, community partners, consultants, and the public.

Work Performed
Primary responsibilities will include, but non exclusively:

Research and policy engagement (50%)

  • Leads ongoing strategic legal and policy research projects to advance CCLI’s policy objectives, working at times with an interdisciplinary scholarly team. Also leads and carries out legal and policy research on mandatory climate-related disclosures for issuers and federally regulated companies, greenwashing, international and national climate-related standards, and transition plans.
  • Conducts and prepares comprehensive analyses used for CCLI policy briefing notes, letters, and submissions.
  • Develops proposed research opportunities and research scopes for consideration and approval by the Director, including identifying research questions, potential areas of inquiry, anticipated outputs, and required resources.
  • Develops proposed research opportunities and research scopes for consideration and approval, including identifying research questions, potential areas of inquiry, anticipated outputs, and required resources.
  • Leads approved legal and policy research projects and independently determines the day-to-day research approach, priorities, methodology, activities, and timelines within the approved scope.
  • Identifies emerging legal, regulatory, policy, and market developments and independently identifies potential research opportunities that align with CCLI's strategic objectives.
  • Identifies research opportunities and analysis gaps, and originates strategic research initiatives that advance CCLI policy objectives and greater organizational objectives.
  • Identifies opportunities for CCLI to participate in government, regulatory, standard-setting, and other public consultations and develops proposed policy submissions for the Director's consideration and approval.
  • Collects policy feedback from CCLI Director, Climate Governance Experts, external consultants, and partners in the ecosystem to better form policy recommendations.
  • Identifies emerging trends in both domestic and international environments that may impact the organization’s objectives and work. By identifying emerging trends, the Senior Policy Researcher can better provide recommendations.
  • Maintains and updates databases that contain policy information, key contact information of senior policymakers, legislators, supervisors, and regulators.
  • Engages independently with academic experts, research partners, practitioners, policymakers, and regulators at the federal and provincial levels, such as the Prime Minister’s Office, Finance Canada, etc., and other subject-matter experts such as Science and Economic Development Canada, Environment and Climate Change Canada, etc., to inform the development and refinement of research questions and approaches.
  • Leads consultations with experts and partners during the development of research projects and incorporates relevant feedback into research scopes and outputs.
  • Conducts legal and policy research, translates complex legal and policy concepts and knowledge into educational blogs for CCLI website.
  • Reviews and quality-assures research and analysis prepared by research assistants and external research partners, including research undertaken with organizations and academic institutes.
  • Oversees research assistants working on CCLI policy-related research projects, including assigning research responsibilities, providing clear research instructions, establishing expectations and timelines, meeting individually with research assistants to discuss project progress, providing feedback and guidance, reviewing the quality and accuracy of completed work, and assessing performance.
  • Coordinates research assistant schedules and workloads to accommodate academic schedules and other commitments while ensuring research activities are completed in accordance with project requirements and timelines.
  • Participates in the interview and selection process for research assistants in collaboration with the Director. Formal hiring decisions and final approval remain with the Director.
  • Reads relevant published papers and reports.
  • Stays well-informed on climate and ESG-related developments.

Ecosystem engagement and thought leadership (40%)

  • Provides legal research to key partners in the sustainable finance ecosystem aligned with our objectives to advance sustainable finance regulations and policies.
  • Independently meets with research partners, policymakers, regulators, standard setters, government representatives, and other stakeholders to discuss CCLI research, emerging policy developments, research opportunities, and areas of collaboration.
  • Builds and maintains excellent relationships with key stakeholders, including partners, consultants, policymakers, and regulators.
  • Identifies opportunities to collaborate with partners focused on advancing climate governance and sustainable finance policies and regulations through policy submissions, presentations, strategic meetings, and more.
  • Collaborates with partners on policy submissions, presentations, strategic meetings, and more, such as the Canadian Sustainability Standards Board and UN Principles for Responsible Investment.
  • Identifies opportunities to present to partners, financial and corporate market participants, and academia to enhance the awareness of CCLI work and advance our policy objectives.
  • Presents CCLI research findings, legal analysis, and policy recommendations to external audiences, including policymakers, regulators, research partners, financial and corporate market participants, academics, and civil society organizations.
  • Acts as a subject-matter expert for climate governance and sustainable finance policy during Chatham House roundtables, conferences, webinars, and other public engagement activities.
  • Represents CCLI in external meetings and policy engagement activities without the Director, including meetings with government and regulatory bodies, research organizations, sustainable finance organizations, academic institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Upholds CCLI's professional reputation and established relationships when representing the organization independently in external engagements.
  • Provides thought leadership in media interviews, blogs, and other relevant ecosystem, communications, and public relations opportunities.
  • Represents CCLI and communicates effectively with media in interviews.

Other responsibilities (10%)

  • Works as part of the CCLI team by contributing to the strategy development and other program activities as required.
  • Contributes to the overall organizational development, including but not exclusively strategic planning, board engagement, communications and event planning, and branding.
  • Other duties may be assigned as required.


Consequence of Error/Judgement
Actions and decisions are critical in ensuring the reputation and success of CCLI. Errors in judgement may cause financial hardship or serious reputational damage. Incorrect decisions/judgments will directly affect CCLI’s reputation.

This role makes professional decisions and recommendations on all aspects of policy research work and is responsible for the quality of CCLI’s research and analysis activities. The Senior Policy Researcher exercises initiative and judgement in establishing priorities and carrying tasks through to completion, and must demonstrate tact and discretion. The person works independently with considerable latitude. Its work is reviewed in terms of achievement of project objectives and overall regard for CCLI objectives. Makes decisions regarding policy research and engagement with key stakeholders. The performance of this position can have a major impact on how the CCLI is perceived by regulators and government bodies, and partners such as for-profit organizations, environmental non-governmental organizations, and civil society.

Error in the performance of duties or inappropriate disclosure of confidential information may adversely affect the image and reputation of CCLI, the Peter A. Allard School of Law, and the University.

Supervision Received
Reports to the Director of the Canada Climate Law Initiative. Works with considerable latitude; research work is reviewed against achievement of project objectives.

Supervision Given
Provides functional supervision and day-to-day direction to research assistants working on CCLI policy-related research projects.

Responsibilities include assigning and coordinating research tasks, providing research instructions and guidance, establishing timelines, meeting with research assistants to review progress, providing feedback, reviewing and quality-assuring completed work, and assessing performance.

May manage student workers.

Minimum Qualifications
Undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline. Minimum of two years of related experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own.
  • Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Law degree (LL.B., J.D.) and master's degree preferred.
  • PhD completed or near completion in corporate and securities law, financial services law, public policy, climate governance, or a related field is an asset.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently identify research opportunities and develop research scopes and proposals.
  • Demonstrated strong analytical, legal research, and policy research skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead research projects from approved scope through completion.
  • Demonstrated ability to critically review and quality-assure research undertaken by research assistants and external research partners.
  • Demonstrated experience engaging with policymakers, regulators, standard setters, academics, research organizations, or other external stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex legal and policy concepts to audiences with varying levels of subject-matter expertise.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgement, discretion, and initiative in external stakeholder engagement.
  • Experience supervising, mentoring, or coordinating research assistants or junior researchers is an asset.
  • Experience in corporate, securities, financial services, climate risk and governance, disclosure, sustainable finance, or related policy areas is an asset.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset.

Definition

Process Management

Customer Focus

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Identity Fusion consultants have worked in the identity management space for over 25 years, dating back to the early days of Netscape. As a thought leader in the identity and access management space, Identity Fusion works with clients across industries including healthcare, financial services, high tech, manufacturing and publishing. Each client has different goals, but they all share one thing in common: the need for a dynamic and robust infrastructure to simplify the processes associated with IAM technologies delivering real business value.

We are seeking a bright, motivated Senior Consultant with a passion for architecting and implementing PingOne AIC, built on the latest technologies. You will work in a fast paced, fun and dynamic environment on a variety of projects. You’ll gain exposure to clients and a variety of needs across multiple industries, collaborate within a high caliber, fast paced project team and help mentor the consultants around you while building world class systems for Fortune 500 clients.

We offer competitive salaries, full benefits, extensive training and mentorship and performance based incentives. You must have the ability to travel, but for the most part work is performed remotely.

Position Overview

As a Senior Consultant, you will lead the design and delivery of identity and access management solutions for enterprise clients built on the Ping Identity Advanced Identity Cloud (AIC) platform. The work is typically remote, though travel may periodically be required. You must be as comfortable at the boardroom table as you are on the whiteboard and keyboard and be able to articulate the business value of identity solutions to executive stakeholders while also configuring and delivering the technical components of an AIC implementation.

As a Senior Consultant, you will own the solution architecture and hands-on delivery for client engagements built on the PingOne Advanced Identity Cloud (AIC) platform, spanning both Identity Management and Access Management workstreams. This includes identity lifecycle management and synchronization across enterprise applications, directories and authoritative sources, as well as authentication, authorization, federation and access orchestration.

This is a senior, client-facing delivery position; you will serve as the technical lead across the engagement lifecycle from discovery and solution design through implementation, integration, go-live and hypercare. The role moves comfortably between hands-on configuration (including identity synchronization, mappings, reconciliation, lifecycle workflows, connectors and integrations and authentication/orchestration journeys) and advisory conversations with client security and identity leadership. As a Senior Consultant you will also provide technical direction and mentorship to junior consultants while ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, supportable and aligned with the client's broader IAM architecture and business requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, configuration and deployment of AIC solutions. This includes journeys/orchestration, authentication trees and authorization policies.
  • Serve as the senior technical lead on client engagements. Be able to perform discovery and requirements sessions, producing solution architecture and design documents and owning delivery through implementation, testing and cutover.
  • Architect and implement single sign-on (SSO), multifactor authentication (MFA), federation (SAML, OAuth 2.0, OIDC) and passwordless authentication (Passkeys/WebAuthn) across web, mobile and native applications.
  • Design and manage identity lifecycle processes (joiner, mover, leaver) integrated with upstream authoritative source(s) and downstream target systems.
  • Integrate AIC with enterprise systems via REST/SOAP APIs, SCIM and custom connectors; script and extend platform capabilities (JavaScript/Groovy, scripted decision nodes).
  • Advise clients on IAM architecture best practices, including RBAC/ABAC models, Zero Trust principles and how AIC's fully managed SaaS model changes cloud/infrastructure responsibilities versus self-managed Ping (PingAM/PingIDM/PingDS) deployments.
  • Troubleshoot complex provisioning, authentication issues across production and pre-production environments; lead root-cause analysis and remediation.
  • Produce clear technical documentation (architecture diagrams, runbooks and configuration standards) and lead knowledge-transfer sessions with client teams.
  • Mentor and technically guide junior and mid-level consultants on engagements; contribute to internal AIC delivery methodology, accelerators and reusable assets.
  • Monitor system performance post-deployment and recommend tuning, scaling or roadmap improvements; stay current on emerging IAM trends and new Ping platform capabilities.
  • Support presales activities as needed, including scoping, level of effort estimation and technical input for proposals and statements of work.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on IAM consulting or engineering experience, including at least 3+ years working directly with AIC in production enterprise environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading full-lifecycle AIC effort, including architecture and design through deployment and hyper care (not just administration).
  • Strong working knowledge of identity and security protocols: SAML, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SCIM, WS-Fed, Kerberos and FIDO2/WebAuthn.
  • Solid understanding of IAM concepts including SSO, MFA, federation, RBAC/ABAC, Zero Trust and lifecycle access management.
  • Working proficiency with REST/SOAP APIs and at least one scripting or programming language commonly used in Ping environments (JavaScript and/or Groovy).
  • Comfort operating within AIC's fully managed SaaS model. This includes implementation across multiple tenant environments, coordination of ESVs (Environment Secrets & Variables), configuration of promotion pipelines and the use of tools such as Frodo for managing and debugging AIC.
  • Proficiency with Git-based version control (Bitbucket, GitHub or GitLab) and CI/CD pipelines for managing IAM configuration-as-code including branching, code review and release workflows.
  • Excellent client-facing communication skills. Be able to translate technical detail for executive stakeholders and translate business requirements into technical designs for engineers.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Security or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote, client-facing consulting environment, including occasional travel to client sites.
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States; U.S. citizenship may be required for certain client engagements (for example, government or regulated-industry contracts).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified Professional – PingOne Advanced Identity Cloud (AIC)
  • Prior experience in a professional services, systems integrator or IAM consultancy environment.
  • Experience with identity data consolidation/virtualization and directory migration projects.
  • Security certifications such as CISSP, CISM or CCSP.

Core Competencies

  • Client-first consulting mindset with strong ownership over engagement outcomes
  • Clear, confident communicator across technical and executive audiences
  • Analytical problem-solver who can operate independently under ambiguity
  • Collaborative mentor who elevates the people around them
  • Comfortable balancing hands-on technical work with advisory responsibilities

jobs.description:
AI Service Analyst

ICS.AI · Remote (UK), occasional travel to Basingstoke and client sites

· Full-time, permanent · £26,500 – £30,000 · Entry level / graduate

Build the AI agents that run our service desk — not reset passwords.

ICS.AI is a UK AI consultancy delivering AI transformation to the public sector — local government, higher education and the wider public estate. Our clients commit to transformation on the strength of savings guarantees, and we are held to contractual service levels once our solutions are live. That makes our service data a commercial asset, not admin overhead.

We are hiring an AI Service Analyst to own the day-to-day operation of our service management function, and to build it properly from the ground up. You will be the single point of coordination between clients raising issues, the delivery and engineering teams who resolve them, and the Customer Success team who own the relationship.

This is a first or second role. You do not need to be able to fix the technology. You need to be able to work out what is actually happening, get it to the right person, and tell the client the truth about it clearly and on time.

What you’ll be doing

  • Running our Zendesk platform end to end — reviewing every incoming ticket, categorising and prioritising it against a consistent ITIL-aligned model, assigning it to the right resolver and chasing it to closure.
  • Early triage on live AI solutions: checking Azure service health, interrogating voice and language platforms, and reproducing what a client is reporting before it consumes a specialist’s time.
  • Problem management and root cause analysis — spotting patterns across incidents, assigning causes, and authoring RCA documents that go to clients.
  • Client communication and service reporting: proactive updates, SLA tracking, the weekly report pack, and service content for monthly and quarterly reviews.
  • Monthly trend analysis across the client portfolio, and the structured feedback loop from live service into our product roadmap.
  • Designing, building, shadow-running and tuning AI agents inside Zendesk for triage, classification and first response — including the guardrails that decide what an agent is never allowed to handle alone.

What makes this different from a service desk role

You will not be resetting passwords. Our tickets concern live AI solutions serving citizens and council staff — conversational assistants, voice services, agents and data platforms. And a genuine part of the job is building AI agents to handle the queue: that is what lets the function absorb a growing client base without growing headcount, and it is the difference between this post and a conventional service desk appointment. It is no-code work, but it needs someone who will iterate patiently rather than accept the first output.

What we’re looking for

We are not screening on a degree classification or a specific subject. What we care about is evidence of the following:

  • Excellent written English — clear, accurate and appropriate for a professional client audience.
  • Strong organisational discipline, and the ability to hold many open items without losing any of them.
  • An analytical mindset; comfortable with numbers and spotting patterns.
  • Confidence and composure in direct contact with clients by email, phone and video, including when they are unhappy.
  • Competence with Microsoft 365, particularly Excel.
  • A genuine interest in AI and in how technology is used in public services.
  • Eligibility to work in the UK. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Nice to have

  • ITIL 4 Foundation — not required at appointment; we will fund it within your first three months.
  • Any exposure to a ticketing platform (Zendesk, ServiceNow, Freshdesk, Jira Service Management), including a placement year.
  • Experience of local government, higher education or the wider public sector.
  • Familiarity with generative AI tools, or any experience of configuring or prompting them.
  • Exposure to chatbot, virtual agent or workflow automation configuration.
  • Basic understanding of cloud concepts, particularly Microsoft Azure, or any exposure to Power BI or similar.

What you don’t need

  • Coding or software engineering ability.
  • Machine learning or data science knowledge — agent building here is configuration and prompting.
  • Infrastructure, networking or telephony engineering skills.
  • Previous line management or commercial experience.

The package

  • £26,500 – £30,000, with progression to the top of the band on completion of ITIL 4 Foundation and your six-month review.
  • Full-time, permanent. Remote within the UK, with occasional travel to Basingstoke and to client sites.
  • A structured twelve-month development framework with reviews at three, six, nine and twelve months, and a described route to Senior AI Service Analyst.
  • Funded ITIL 4 Foundation certification.
  • £100 per month WFH Allowance
  • Vitality Healthcare Plan
  • Pension Scheme
  • 25 days holiday

Whether the opportunity involves lead quality, nurture, application completion, creative, or Sales follow-up, you will be expected to contribute proactively and coordinate improvements across teams.

Adaptability is equally important. Nexford operates in an evolving environment where business priorities, programs, messaging, and enrollment needs can change. You must be comfortable working through ambiguity, reassessing plans as new information becomes available, and communicating tradeoffs clearly. We value someone who raises concerns constructively, proposes solutions, and follows through when priorities shift.

This is an individual contributor position with direct responsibility for execution and project ownership. You will work with internal specialists and external partners, respect their expertise, and remain accountable for moving your initiatives forward. You do not need to execute every function yourself, but you must be willing to work across functions to deliver enrollment results.

What you will own:

Paid media strategy and execution

  • Plan, launch, manage, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, and other relevant channels.
  • Own campaign structure, targeting, bidding, budget pacing, tracking requirements, and ongoing optimization.
  • Build monthly media plans aligned with enrollment priorities, historical performance, seasonality, and the applicant decision cycle.
  • Allocate spend based on qualified demand, downstream conversion, and acquisition efficiency.
  • Maintain a prioritized testing plan for audiences, creative, offers, and landing pages.

Funnel performance and demand generation

  • Monitor the journey from lead generation through application starts, completed applications, and enrollment.
  • Identify where prospects drop off and coordinate improvements with the teams responsible.
  • Own NAM campaign and audience requirements for nurture initiatives, including segmentation, messaging, and conversion goals.
  • Partner with Marketing Operations on implementation, testing, and measurement of nurture and automation.
  • Evaluate campaign performance beyond lead volume and cost per lead.

Sales and Admissions alignment

  • Maintain regular communication with Sales and Admissions on lead quality, follow-up, objections, and conversion barriers.
  • Use feedback and funnel data to recommend campaign, messaging, and targeting adjustments.
  • Coordinate campaign launches with team capacity and relevant enrollment dates.
  • Bring clear recommendations and follow through on agreed actions.

Creative and conversion optimization

  • Develop clear creative briefs with audience insights, hooks, messaging, calls to action, and testing hypotheses.
  • Work with Creative to produce and improve campaign assets.
  • Partner with the website and digital teams on landing pages, forms, and conversion experiments.
  • Share performance feedback that helps teams understand what to improve and why.

Reporting, forecasting, and accountability

  • Maintain accurate dashboards and deliver reporting on the agreed cadence.
  • Explain results in the context of spend, seasonality, attribution, campaign maturity, and conversion timing.
  • Contribute to enrollment forecasts and clearly communicate assumptions, risks, and resource needs.
  • Translate reporting into decisions, experiments, and next steps.
  • Keep Asana tasks, documentation, deadlines, and project status current.

Vendor and cross-functional project ownership

  • Manage relevant paid media and demand generation vendors, including briefs, deliverables, timelines, and performance.
  • Own assigned initiatives from planning through completion, coordinating contributions from other teams.
  • Flag blockers early and propose practical solutions.
  • Support enrollment-focused webinars, partnerships, and events where campaign expertise is needed, with responsibilities and priorities agreed in advance.

AI-enabled efficiency

  • Use appropriate AI tools to support research, analysis, campaign development, and routine workflows.
  • Review outputs for accuracy, brand alignment, and suitability before use.
  • Assess AI applications based on their contribution to efficiency and marketing outcomes.

What you bring

  • At least four years of B2C hands-on performance marketing or demand generation experience.
  • Demonstrated experience managing paid B2C campaigns targeting U.S. audiences.
  • Strong working knowledge of Google Ads and Meta Ads; experience with LinkedIn Ads is a plus.
  • Evidence of improving downstream conversion and acquisition efficiency, beyond generating inexpensive leads.
  • Experience working with Sales on a considered-purchase journey or a multi-stage conversion funnel.
  • Proficiency with HubSpot or a comparable CRM, GA4, campaign attribution, and reporting tools.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to build realistic plans from historical data.
  • Experience briefing creative teams, coordinating vendors, and managing projects across functions.
  • Clear communication, reliable follow-through, and comfort raising concerns constructively.
  • Higher education or adult learner acquisition experience is preferred.

How success will be measured

Targets will be established using historical performance, available budget, sales capacity, and conversion timing. Measures will include:

  • Qualified lead and application generation.
  • Application completion and lead-to-enrollment conversion.
  • Cost per qualified lead, completed application, and enrollment.
  • Budget pacing and forecast accuracy.
  • Results from creative, audience, landing page, and nurture experiments.
  • Timely delivery, documentation, and completion of agreed projects.
  • Effective collaboration with Sales, Admissions, and Marketing Operations.

What to expect

You’ll join a motivated, creative, and innovative marketing team that enjoys testing ideas, solving challenges, and finding better ways to reach learners. You’ll have room to bring your perspective, shape campaigns, and see the impact of your work.

At Nexford University, you’ll help expand access to education built around the needs of today’s learners and employers. As an online university serving a global community, Nexford brings together people who believe education can open doors to new opportunities. For a marketer, that means meaningful stories to tell, new ideas to explore, and the chance to connect learners with programs that support their ambitions. You’ll join an international team where creativity, fresh perspectives, and collaboration help shape what comes next.

Collaboration goes beyond Marketing. You’ll work closely with Sales, Admissions, Creative, and Marketing Operations to turn ideas into action and improve the enrollment journey.

As Nexford grows, you’ll help the team explore new opportunities and adapt campaigns to changing learner and business needs. The Head of Marketing provides strategic direction and helps align priorities, while you bring initiative, hands-on execution, and ownership of your projects.

Company Overview:

Truegenics Pte Ltd is a leading ecommerce company based in Singapore with a track record of over US$218M in online product sales. We specialise in e-retailing our own brand of health supplements to a global audience. We strive to create value and make a positive difference in the world, one life at a time. We believe that even the smallest action can define one’s destiny, and are committed to the creation of products that enhance the lives of our consumers.

Mission of the Role:

The mission of this role is to drive profitable e-commerce growth by executing and optimizing high-performing media buys across platforms, responsibly managing four-figure daily budgets to hit target ROAS while maintaining a great user experience (including weekend performance reviews). This role goes beyond adjusting budgets and switching ads on or off. You’ll help find customer angles, shape creative tests, and give specific feedback to our copywriting and creative teams. You’ll be accountable for the performance of your projects while working with the Media Buying Lead on priorities and broader strategy.

This role starts off as a 6-month contract role, with the possibility of conversion to a permanent position subject to individual performance and business needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own direct response projects on Meta. Plan, launch, manage, and scale campaigns for assigned products or offers, with clear targets for acquisition and profitability.
  • Turn data into decisions. Monitor spend, revenue, ROAS, CPA, conversion rate, average order value, and other relevant funnel metrics. Diagnose performance changes and propose actions based on the evidence.
  • Build a testing plan. Develop hypotheses, prioritise tests, define what success looks like, and use the results to decide what to scale, revise, or stop.
  • Find angles and guide creative development. Research customers, competitors, and market trends to identify fresh angles and hooks. Brief copywriters and designers, then give practical feedback on ad copy, images, and videos using performance data and your understanding of the audience.
  • Manage budgets responsibly and optimise for ROI. Allocate spend across campaigns and tests, respond to performance changes, and scale what works while meeting profitability and return on investment (ROI) targets.
  • Work across the customer journey. Look beyond ad metrics to identify issues with landing pages, offers, checkout, tracking, or attribution, and work with the relevant teams to resolve them.
  • Communicate clearly. Share concise performance updates, explain what you’ve learned, and recommend the next actions for each project.
  • Maintain campaign quality. Follow Meta advertising policies, ensure ads provide a positive user experience, and review live campaigns regularly, including weekend performance checks when required.
  • Handle any other ad-hoc projects or tasks as assigned.

Key Requirements:

  • Degree or higher (preferably in business/marketing or a related field) with 2 years of experience running marketing campaigns for e-commerce stores to generate revenue.
  • Strong proven knowledge of media-buying platforms and its compliance/guidelines such as Facebook, Bing, and Google Ads.
  • At least 2 years and 1 year of hands-on experience managing Facebook Ads and Google Ads respectively.
  • Analytical mindset and a self-starter with the ability to develop solutions and next steps for campaign testing.
  • Positive and can-do attitude when handling new marketing campaigns that require rigorous testing.
  • Sense of ownership in one’s performance and its impact on company’s success which includes responsibly managing a 4-figure media buying daily budget and achieving the target ROAS.
  • Conversant in English and possess a creative mindset which will be useful for creating and writing advertising assets in the form of copy, video, and images that suit the target audience.
  • Comfortable using AI tools to speed up research, explore customer angles, develop testing ideas, and analyse campaign results, while checking outputs against actual performance data and advertising guidelines.

Key Technical Skills:

  • Excellent understanding of Facebook Platforms
  • Skills and experience with programs such as Canva and Photoshop are advantageous.
  • Good understanding of media analytics tools such as Google Analytics UA & GA4.
  • Familiarity with other tracking platforms such as Voluum, Hyros, Redtrack is a bonus.
  • Experience with Microsoft Tools

Remote Working Setup

  • A computer with suitable performance.
  • At least two monitor screens, including the laptop screen.
  • A noise-cancelling headset with microphone and a webcam.
  • A designated workstation in a quiet, conducive environment.
  • Reliable power and internet connectivity.

The Ideal Candidate

You’re a hands-on media buyer who enjoys the challenge of growing sales profitably. You’ve managed e-commerce campaigns on Meta, know how to make decisions when performance changes, and are comfortable being accountable for a four-figure daily budget. You can explain what the numbers are telling you, what you’ll test next, and when it makes sense to scale or pull back.

You bring more than platform expertise. You’re curious about customers, offers, and the reasons people buy. You can spot promising angles, brief copywriters and designers clearly, and use campaign results to make creative feedback more specific. When an ad performs poorly, you look across the full customer journey before deciding what needs to change.

You take ownership of your projects, communicate your thinking concisely, and stay attentive to live campaign performance, including weekend checks when needed.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Entertainment
jobs.excerpt: Job Type: Full-timeReports to: Co-CEOLocation: Remote within the contiguous U.
jobs.description:
Job Type: Full-time

Reports to: Co-CEO

Location: Remote within the contiguous U.S. We have a preference for candidates based in or near the Los Angeles area, given the role’s engagement with RTT’s Entertainment community. The role will periodically require travel to Los Angeles for in-person programming and/or availability for evening events and programs aligned to Pacific Time.

About Resetting the Table

Resetting the Table (RTT) equips leaders and communities from every corner of American life to counter toxic polarization and build a shared society and democracy. Through rigorous training, courageous dialogue, and empathy-generating media content, we enable Americans to transform differences into an engine of strengthened relationship, trust, and problem-solving in our country and communities. RTT’s trainings and forums have directly reached more than 100,000 participants across the U.S., many of them industry-shaping TV writers and executives, faith leaders, higher education administrators, and other leaders positioned to make far-reaching culture change and indirectly impact millions more. Informed by combined expertise in the fields of mediation, conflict transformation, trauma therapy, and social research, our methodology for building “healthy conflict” in communities is nationally recognized and highly sought after.

RTT’s renowned Multivocal Storytelling framework equips Hollywood creatives and executives with tools to meet one of the industry’s most urgent challenges: telling stories that resonate across audiences in a polarized America, while directly engaging charged issues that shape viewers’ lives. In this volatile moment, this position offers an exciting opportunity to play a meaningful role in harnessing the power of storytelling and popular entertainment to rehumanize across divides while strengthening stories and broadening reach.

RTT’s work is meaningful, complex, and deeply rewarding — you will contribute to transforming societal conflict while working alongside exceptionally thoughtful and caring colleagues. At RTT, we see the motivation, growth, and well-being of our team members as a critical ingredient to our success. We are committed to fostering a workplace environment that models our work in the world: welcoming, bold, collaborative, supportive, and creating the conditions to bring out people’s best contributions.

The Opportunity

Resetting the Table (RTT) is seeking a Managing Director, Entertainment to lead the ongoing translation of our Entertainment program’s ambitious vision and strategy into coordinated action, overseeing the team and systems to drive high impact at a pivotal moment of growth. You will supervise three seasoned leaders rich with strategic insights, expertise, and relationships in the industry, leveraging their strengths and stewarding team cohesion and shared direction. This is a role for someone who is energized by building the conditions to support teams to excel and execute at their highest level — a highly organized orchestrator and skilled manager who turns big picture commitments into ongoing workflows and implementation. You will bring deep management experience and knowledge of the entertainment industry to a mission-driven organization with a bold vision for the role popular entertainment can play in countering our societal crisis of division and distrust.

What You’ll Do

This is a leadership role focused on overseeing a talented team, driving the structures and actionable plans that enable its success, and accelerating RTT’s impact in catalyzing humanizing stories in TV, film, and digital content that bridge divides. Your work will include:

Team Leadership & Management (50%)

  • Lead the Entertainment team to support its greatest strategic impact, working closely with senior leadership and synthesizing members’ distinct expertise and strategic perspectives toward shared goals
  • Partner with each team member to transform big-picture strategies into focused workplans through regular team meetings and one-on-ones with direct reports
  • Establish team rhythms and accountability practices that create visibility into progress, surface challenges, and keep workstreams moving forward
  • Serve as a thought partner and sounding board to the co-CEOs and senior leadership, synthesizing information across workstreams, surfacing opportunities and needs, and ensuring that day-to-day decisions stay aligned with the organization’s longer-term goals

Strategy Execution & Operationalization (30%)

  • Translate the Entertainment program’s strategies into roadmaps for execution, establishing ongoing priorities, decision-making processes, and timelines to bring the vision to life
  • Oversee and refine the systems that enable the team to manage complex work effectively, including breaking projects into tasks and deliverables, delegating ownership, tracking progress, and following through across program design and delivery, follow-on action items, and the team’s portfolio of relationships
  • Steward the production and delivery of RTT's entertainment-facing materials and communications, ensuring work is strategically aligned and reflects a high standard of excellence
  • Partner with RTT's development team to ensure capturing of the evidence, stories, and relationship data that demonstrate program impact and enhance funder reporting

Alumni Engagement Strategy (20%)

  • Hone a strategic approach to activating RTT’s alumni network, strengthening the systems, data, and engagement practices needed to deepen relationships, identify high-value opportunities, and deepen impact and connections across the industry
  • Oversee the creation of meaningful pathways for alumni to stay engaged with RTT, integrating alumni engagement into the Entertainment team’s priority work and creating opportunities for alumni to deepen their learning and collaboration with RTT
  • Continuously assess and evolve the alumni engagement strategy, identifying opportunities to increase participation and maximize the network’s contribution to RTT’s cultural impact and footprint in the entertainment industry

Who You Are

  • You're the person who makes things run. You look at a complex web of people, timelines, and deliverables and instinctively start building the structure that moves it all forward with a high bar for excellence.
  • You know the entertainment industry from the inside. You speak the language, understand the dynamics, and know how the industry moves. You can look at our team and alumni community and see the depth of experience and potential for strong impact it represents.
  • You bring out the best in the people around you. You lead by partnering—setting clear direction, checking in with purpose, and making sure your team has what they need to do their strongest work.
  • You are motivated by the opportunity to build something exceptional. You care deeply about quality, not just completion. You notice what could be better, ask thoughtful questions, and push toward stronger strategy, clearer execution, and better outcomes. You bring both ambition and discernment to the work, knowing when to move quickly, when to go deeper, and when something is good enough to move forward.
  • You're as strong in a room as you are behind the scenes. You can represent an organization with credibility at industry events and in Hollywood's professional circles, and you're just as effective at supporting a team to execute at its highest potential and oversee the systems that keep the work running day to day.
  • You believe in RTT’s mission and Multivocal Storytelling framework. You care about overcoming societal polarization and uplifting dignity, authenticity, and complexity across lines of difference. You believe it is crucial for more Americans to communicate and collaborate constructively across differences in backgrounds and ideological views. You proactively pursue opportunities to learn from divergent perspectives.

What You Bring

  • A track record of managing teams and driving forward complex, multi-stakeholder work with excellence and discipline
  • Professional experience in or alongside the entertainment industry, with a working understanding of the landscape, the roles, and how projects move from development through production
  • Experience overseeing and developing systems and processes that help teams prioritize, create action plans, track progress, and make decisions
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize information from across functions and translate it into clear goals and deliverables
  • Excellent people manager and organizational skills with the demonstrated ability to oversee multiple workstreams and support a team in delivering at its strongest
  • Experience working closely with senior executives or organizational leaders in a high-trust capacity

Role Logistics:

  • Evening availability: This role requires periodic availability and participation in evening Entertainment program events, often aligned to Pacific Time.
  • Travel: If not based in the Los Angeles area, this role requires periodic travel to LA, as well as occasional travel to other locations.

How to Apply

We know there are great candidates who may not check every box, and you may bring valuable skills and experiences we haven’t considered. If this role excites you and aligns with your values and aspirations, we strongly encourage you to apply and tell us about yourself.

We will review applications on a rolling basis. The application consists of three parts:

  • Resume
  • Cover Letter, addressing:
    • Why you're drawn to RTT's mission and Entertainment program
    • Why you're the right person for this role at this moment in your career
  • Short answer responses (a robust paragraph):
    • What does great people management look like to you? Give us a specific example of a time you put it into practice.
    • Describe a time you worked closely with a senior leader or executive to turn a vision or strategic priority into action. What did that partnership look like, and what made it effective?

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for the Managing Director, Entertainment is $125,000–$155,000, commensurate with experience. This is a full-time position with benefits. Typical office hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with some obligations taking place in the evenings and on weekends and periodic travel.

Benefits package includes:

  • Health benefits, life insurance, and short- and long-term disability
  • Generous package of vacation, sick, and personal days, along with paid time off for federal and religious holidays each year
  • Paid parental leave
  • Reimbursement for home office expenses of up to $1,000
  • 403(b) plan with 3% employer contribution
  • A highly collaborative, caring team

At Resetting the Table, we celebrate differences of background, identity, and viewpoint for the benefit of our employees, work, and community. RTT is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender, age, religion, ideology, national origin, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition, or any protected category prohibited by local, state, or federal laws. All aspects of employment are decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and organizational need.

Salary: $125,000-$155,000
